issues.failure_explanation: Definition def-NumSol-SLDG takes both the unknown and the test functions in all of H_0(Omega_K), i.e. essentially all of L^2(Omega_K). It uses no polynomial space and no quadrature or interpolation of psi. The 'scheme' therefore just reproduces the exact transported (pulled-back) function at each t_n. The mesh and the degree P play no role. The paper claims existence, uniqueness and stability of the CSLDG numerical solutions and scheme. What it establishes concerns only this idealized exact evolution operator, not the finite-dimensional DG scheme of Section 2 or its A1/A2 quadrature implementations.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must redefine the scheme with trial and test functions in the piecewise polynomial space V_h^P. It must then prove solvability and stability there, for example via L^2-projection contraction and a flow-Jacobian bound, and either analyse or explicitly exclude the quadrature/interpolation versions A1/A2.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised theoretical contribution (well-posedness and unconditional stability of the CSLDG numerical scheme) does not cover any actual DG discretization. The Section 3 theorems say nothing about the computed solutions.

issues.failure_explanation: A support is the closure of the non-vanishing set. Points of supp Psi, such as boundary points or interior zeros, can have Psi = 0, and likewise for psi. So both inclusions are argued through a false equivalence between 'x in support' and 'function nonzero at x'. The intermediate claims are false even though the final identity holds.

Counterexample: d=1, A=x gives psi(x,t1)=Psi(x e^{t2-t1}), so ||psi(.,t1)||_p^p = e^{-(t2-t1)} ||Psi||_p^p. diagnostic_evidence.quote: becomes a Hilbert space with compact support on the bounded domain

issues.failure_explanation: H_0(Omega) requires supp f to be compactly contained in Omega. A function whose support is all of the closure of Omega_i (e.g. a DG polynomial nonzero up to the boundary) is not in H_0(Omega_i). Moreover, this H_0 is not closed in L^2: indicator functions of interior subdomains converge to chi_Omega, whose support is not compact in Omega. Hence it is not a Hilbert space. The membership claims U_i, U_h, U~_K, Psi in H_0 are therefore unjustified.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which is different from the schemes in \cite{ref1,ref4}

issues.failure_explanation: The x-sweep enforces the 1D invariant only on the K_y+1 lines y = [Gg]^y_s. Multiplying by the inverse of the generalized Vandermonde matrix [Phi]^y_s constructs the unique degree-K_y polynomial matching these nodal results, which is exactly Lagrange interpolation in y (and likewise in x for the y-sweep). The method therefore interpolates at every dimension switch, and the claimed distinction from the nodal splitting of ref1/ref4 is not real.
